2027-03-13.title: Saturday of the Fourth Week of Lent
readings: I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter
O Lord, my God, in you I take refuge
Does the Messiah come from Galilee?
2027-03-13.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-03-13.verse: The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
theo: Jeremiah, the prophet of tears, discovers that people from his own town, Anathoth, are plotting to kill him. “It was the LORD who made it known to me, and I knew.” Until then he had not suspected anything: “But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter.” They said: “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will no longer be remembered!” Jeremiah does not take revenge with his own hands. He places his cause before the LORD of hosts, who judges righteously and tries the heart and the mind: “to you I have committed my cause.” His cry for retribution is honest, but the deeper movement is trust. The Church reads this passage on the threshold of Passiontide because Jeremiah is a living image of Christ, the true Lamb of God, who will be led to the slaughter and will not open his mouth, and who will commit his cause, and his spirit, into the Father's hands. The Psalm prays it with him: “O LORD my God, in you I take refuge.”

In the Gospel Jesus has spoken on the last day of the feast of Booths, and the crowd is divided. Some say: “This is really the prophet.” Others: “This is the Messiah.” Others object: the Messiah must come from Bethlehem, not Galilee. The irony is that Jesus was born in Bethlehem, but they do not know it. The Temple police, sent to arrest him, come back empty-handed. Asked why, they give one of the most beautiful testimonies in the Gospel: “Never has anyone spoken like this!” They have been disarmed by a word. The Pharisees scorn them and the crowd: “this crowd, which does not know the law… they are accursed.” Then one voice rises from among the rulers: Nicodemus, “who had gone to Jesus before,” by night. He does not yet confess Jesus openly; he only asks for fairness: “Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing… does it?” They mock him too. But this small courage will grow: on Good Friday Nicodemus will come to the cross carrying a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes for the burial of Jesus. Lent asks us: will we let Jesus' word disarm us, and will we find courage, even a little, to speak for him?
outline: Ask: has a word ever stopped you in your tracks?
Point 2 · Never has anyone spoken like this
From a question to a hundred pounds of myrrh.
“O LORD my God, in you I take refuge.”
live: Bring to God one injustice you have suffered, and give up the wish for revenge.
Like Nicodemus, speak up gently for someone who is being judged without a hearing.
2027-03-13.prayer: Lord God, you saw Jeremiah led like a lamb to the slaughter, and you sent your Son, the true Lamb, to take away the sin of the world. Let his word disarm our hearts, and give us the courage of Nicodemus to speak for him and for the truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we hear: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. The gentle lamb of Jeremiah's lament is fulfilled in Christ, who gives himself to us on the altar.

quick: Jeremiah, plotted against, is like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, a figure of Christ.
The Temple police return without arresting Jesus: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
Nicodemus speaks a small word of fairness, and later honours Jesus at his burial.
2027-03-13.action: Speak up today for someone who is being judged unfairly.
2027-03-13.question: Where do I need the courage of Nicodemus?

family.explain: Some soldiers were sent to arrest Jesus. But when they heard him speak, they could not do it. They went back and said: nobody has ever spoken like this man! Jesus' words are so full of truth and love that they change hearts.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated unfairly.
family.ask: Ask: “Which words of Jesus do you love the most?”

illus: In a college staff room in Ernakulam, colleagues were mocking a young teacher who had been accused, without evidence, of copying a paper. An older professor, quiet and shy, put down his cup and said only: has anyone asked her? The room went silent. The young teacher later said that sentence saved her career, and her faith in people.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, no one has ever spoken like you. Let your word disarm us and give us courage. Amen.
share: I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter (Jeremiah 11:19). Where do I see Christ the Lamb in those who suffer today?
Never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). Which word of Jesus has disarmed me?
Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). For whom must I speak up?
pm.resp: O Lord, my God, in you I take refuge.
interc: For those plotted against or betrayed by their own people.
For police and soldiers, that they may serve justice and protect the innocent.
For those who are judged without a hearing, that truth may come to light.
For timid believers, that they may grow in courage like Nicodemus.
For our group, that the word of Jesus may change our hearts.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, the Lamb, whose words are spirit and life. Make us his witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah discovers that people from his own town want to kill him. He says: I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter (Jeremiah 11:19). He does not take revenge. He says to God: to you I have committed my cause. In Jeremiah the Church sees Jesus, the true Lamb, who goes to his death without hatred.

In the Gospel the Temple police are sent to arrest Jesus. They come back with empty hands. Why? Because, they say, never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). They came to bind him, and his word bound their hearts.

Then Nicodemus, who once came to Jesus by night, speaks up. It is only a small question: our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing, does it? But it is a beginning. On Good Friday this same Nicodemus will come openly to bury Jesus with myrrh and aloes.

Next Sunday the Church enters the last two weeks of Lent. Let the word of Jesus disarm us. And let us find the courage, even a little at first, to speak for him and for those who are judged unfairly. Amen.
kids: Children, some men were sent to catch Jesus. But when they heard him speak, they could not do it! They said: no one ever spoke like him. Jesus' words are full of love. Let us listen to them carefully at Mass tomorrow.

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
The gentle lamb, the word that disarms, and the small courage of Nicodemus.

q: But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Give one hurt you carry to God tonight, and pray for the one who caused it.

points.h: Never has anyone spoken like this
q: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read one chapter of John's Gospel slowly each day until Palm Sunday.

q: God is my shield, who saves the upright in heart.
Nicodemus, who had at first come to Jesus by night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about a hundred pounds.
points.apply: Say one word for Christ or for fairness this week where you would normally stay silent.

concl: Jeremiah, the gentle lamb, points to Christ the Lamb of God.
The word of Jesus disarms hearts, and small courage grows into faithful love.
2027-03-13.resolve: Speak one honest word for Christ or for justice this week.
